title: OpenFarm Slicer Provisioning Manifest
description: Maintainer-authored declaration of which (engine, version, platform) slicer builds to fetch into the application's bundled slicer directory, and the exact URL to fetch each from. Consumed only by the dev/build-time provisioning tool (tools/provision-slicers) — never read by the running application (FR-012/FR-018). The tool never derives or guesses an asset URL from a naming pattern: each engine's release asset naming can and does change between versions, so the manifest itself is the sole source of truth — copy the real link from the engine's GitHub releases page for each platform you want. Each platform pins its own version independently (schemaVersion 3) — different platforms commonly need different versions pinned, e.g. because a given release has a platform-specific regression.

schemaVersion.description: Manifest format version for forward-compat; current = 3 (each platform build carries its own version; schemaVersion 2's single entry-level version shared across all platforms is no longer supported).

slicers.description: Desired set of slicers to bundle. Append-only across releases by product commitment (FR-008a) — entries are added, never removed.

platform.description: Target host platform for the fetched build (FR-009/FR-010).

version.description: Maintainer-chosen display version (FR-005) for this specific platform's build — stored/shown verbatim everywhere (bundle directory name, discovery, pickers, recorded values). It need not match the engine's literal upstream release tag; a maintainer may use a friendlier marketed string instead (e.g. "2.7.1" for a Bambu Studio build whose actual tag/asset-embedded string is "02.07.01.57"). It does need to stay a dotted-numeric shape (e.g. "2.2.0", "2.5.59.13", "01.10.00.00") for "newest" ordering to work meaningfully, and must stay stable once a build has shipped. Different platforms are not required to share the same version string — e.g. macOS may need to stay pinned behind Linux/Windows if a given release regressed only on macOS (or vice versa).

assetUrl.description: The exact download URL for this platform's build of the pinned version — copied verbatim from the engine's GitHub releases page (the asset filename/naming convention is not assumed or derived by the tool, since it can change between releases).

builds.description: Per-platform (version, download URL) pin for this engine. A platform omitted here is simply not provisioned for this entry (not a failure, FR-015). Platforms are independent: they may pin different versions of the same engine.

notes.description: Optional free-text maintainer note (e.g. why this version is pinned, or why platforms diverge).

slicers.notes: Pinned to 2.3.1 on every platform: 2.3.2 through the current latest (2.4.2) segfault (SIGSEGV) in Print::apply() whenever a machine settings file and a process settings file are loaded together via --load-settings, reproduced with OrcaSlicer's own unmodified shipped presets. See docs/superpowers/plans/im-running-in-macos-cuddly-matsumoto.md for the investigation.
PrusaSlicer-fork CLI form — see SuperSlicerInvocation. SuperSlicer doesn't consistently publish macOS builds, so no MacOs build here.
